profile.name: AM Ghazanfar
profile.writeup:
Allah Mohammad Ghazanfar, a promising young cricketer from Afghanistan, has quickly made a name for himself with his impressive bowling skills. Known for his off-break deliveries, Ghazanfar has been compared to the renowned Afghan spinner Mujeeb Zadran.


His journey began in the Paktia Province, where he transitioned from a fast bowler to a spin bowler under the guidance of former Afghanistan captain Dawlat Ahmadzai. Ghazanfar's bowling prowess was evident during his debut for the Mis Ainak Knights in the Afghan Shpageeza Cricket League, where he took 1-27 in four overs, followed by a four-wicket haul in his second match. His performance in the 2024 Under-19 Cricket World Cup was notable, particularly his 3-29 against New Zealand, showcasing his potential on the international stage.


Ghazanfar's bowling style is characterized by his ability to maintain a tight line and length, making him a challenging opponent for the batters. His adaptability to different pitch conditions and his knack for picking up crucial wickets have been key to his success. In the 2024 ODI series against Zimbabwe, he claimed a five-wicket haul, conceding just 33 runs, further cementing his reputation as a formidable bowler. His best bowling figures in ODIs stand at 6-26 against Bangladesh, highlighting his capability to deliver match-winning performances.


While Ghazanfar's batting contributions have been limited, his primary role as a bowler has been instrumental in his team's successes. In the domestic circuit, he has played for teams like the Rawalpindi Raiders in the Pakistan Junior League and the Band-e-Amir Dragons in the Shpageeza Cricket League, where he consistently delivered with the ball. His performances in the ACC Men's T20 Emerging Teams Asia Cup, where he took multiple two-wicket hauls, demonstrate his consistency and potential to excel in the shortest format of the game.


At just 15, Ghazanfar created headlines as the youngest player to enter the IPL auction, though he went unsold that year. His breakthrough came in 2024 when Kolkata Knight Riders brought him in as a replacement for Mujeeb Ur Rahman. Since then, he has been a familiar face in franchise cricket, turning out for Colombo Strikers in the 2024 Lanka Premier League, and later joining Rangpur Riders in 2025. His growing reputation as a spinner saw him snapped up by Mumbai Indians for the 2025 IPL, but an untimely injury kept him out of action. By March 2025, he bounced back with another opportunity, signing with Derbyshire for the Vitality Blast.


Building on his consistent performances and the guidance of Afghanistan’s senior spinners, Ghazanfar earned a spot in the Asia Cup held in the UAE, where he featured in a couple of games. With a bright start, youth on his side, and immense potential, Allah Mohammad Ghazanfar stands out as one of Afghanistan’s most exciting prospects.
